sentences.sentence: Hydrochlorothiazide is a thiazide diuretic , often called a water pill, used to treat high blood pressure and to reduce a build-up of fluid in the body ( edema ).
It works by making the kidneys pass more salt and water out of the body, so you urinate more.
Hydrochlorothiazide is often shortened to HCTZ on prescriptions and medical records.
It is available as a tablet, capsule, and liquid (suspension) taken by mouth and is usually taken once or twice a day.
Hydrochlorothiazide is available as:
oral tablet (12.5 mg, 25 mg, and 50 mg)
oral capsule (12.5 mg)
powder for oral suspension (10 mg/mL)
Hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ) brand names included HydroDIURIL tablets (discontinued), Esidrix (discontinued), and Microzide capsules (discontinued); now generic tablets and capsules are available.
The brand name of hydrochlorothiazide oral suspension is Inzirqo.
Hydrochlorothiazide is also an ingredient in many combination blood pressure medicines, including with losartan, lisinopril, valsartan, and more.
Hydrochlorothiazide works by inhibiting the kidneys from reabsorbing sodium and chloride, so more salt and water leave the body in the urine, which helps reduce excess fluid buildup (edema).
Exactly how thiazides lower blood pressure is not fully understood.
The early effect is thought to come from a drop in blood volume.
With longer-term use, blood volume returns towards normal while the blood vessels themselves offer less resistance to blood flow.
Hydrochlorothiazide does not usually change blood pressure that is already normal.
Hydrochlorothiazide is a thiazide diuretic.
Do not take hydrochlorothiazide if you are unable to pass urine (anuria), or if you are allergic to hydrochlorothiazide or to other sulfonamide-derived medicines (sometimes called sulfa drugs).
Before you start HCTZ, tell your doctor if you have or have ever had:
kidney disease or reduced kidney function
liver disease, including cirrhosis
diabetes
gout or high uric acid levels
high cholesterol or high triglycerides
high calcium levels or a parathyroid gland disorder
low potassium or low sodium levels
lupus (systemic lupus erythematosus)
glaucoma
an allergy to sulfa medicines or to penicillin
Also tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding.
Hydrochlorothiazide may cause jaundice or bleeding problems in a newborn.
It can also pass into breast milk and may cause serious side effects in a nursing baby, so you and your doctor should decide whether you will take this medicine or breastfeed.
Hydrochlorothiazide can lower the levels of potassium, sodium, magnesium and chloride in your blood.
Low potassium (hypokalemia) is the most common of these and is more likely at higher doses, during rapid fluid loss, if you have severe cirrhosis, or after long-term use..
Your doctor will check your blood before you start and at intervals during treatment.
Contact your doctor if you have any of the following, which can be signs of a fluid or salt imbalance:
dry mouth, thirst, or unusual weakness or tiredness
dry mouth, thirst, or unusual weakness or tiredness
drowsiness, restlessness or confusion
drowsiness, restlessness or confusion
muscle pain, cramps or muscle fatigue
muscle pain, cramps or muscle fatigue
fast heartbeat
fast heartbeat
passing much less urine than usual
passing much less urine than usual
nausea or vomiting
nausea or vomiting
seizures
seizures
HCTZ reduces the fluid volume in your body, which can lead to sudden kidney injury.
The risk is higher if you have chronic kidney disease, heart failure, or are already low on fluid.
If you have liver disease, small changes in fluid and salt balance can trigger a serious complication called hepatic coma.
Your doctor will monitor your kidney function and watch for changes in alertness.

sentences.subsection_title: Sudden vision changes need urgent care
sentences.sentence: Rarely, hydrochlorothiazide causes sudden short-sightedness (acute myopia) and a sharp rise in pressure inside the eye (acute angle-closure glaucoma), usually within hours to weeks of starting the medicine.

sentences.subsection_title: Sudden vision changes need urgent care
sentences.sentence: Stop taking it and get medical help immediately if your vision drops suddenly or your eye hurts.

sentences.subsection_title: Sudden vision changes need urgent care
sentences.sentence: Left untreated, this can cause permanent loss of vision.

sentences.subsection_title: Sudden vision changes need urgent care
sentences.sentence: A history of allergy to sulfa medicines or penicillin may increase the risk.

sentences.subsection_title: Blood sugar, cholesterol, uric acid and calcium
sentences.sentence: Hydrochlorothiazide can raise blood sugar, cholesterol, triglycerides, uric acid and calcium.

sentences.subsection_title: Blood sugar, cholesterol, uric acid and calcium
sentences.sentence: Your diabetes medicine or insulin dose may need adjusting, and diabetes that was previously unnoticed can become apparent during treatment.

sentences.subsection_title: Blood sugar, cholesterol, uric acid and calcium
sentences.sentence: The rise in uric acid is related to the dose and can cause gout or make existing gout worse.

sentences.subsection_title: Blood sugar, cholesterol, uric acid and calcium
sentences.sentence: Because the medicine also affects calcium, it is stopped before parathyroid function tests, so tell any doctor arranging tests that you take it.

sentences.subsection_title: Blood sugar, cholesterol, uric acid and calcium
sentences.sentence: Your doctor will check these levels from time to time.
Long-term use of hydrochlorothiazide is linked to a small increase in the risk of non-melanoma skin cancer, mainly squamous cell carcinoma.

In a large safety study the increase was about 1 extra case per 16,000 people per year, rising to about 1 extra case per 6,700 people per year among white patients who had taken a total of 50,000 mg or more.
Protect your skin from the sun, wear protective clothing and use sunscreen, avoid sunlamps and tanning beds, and have regular skin checks.
Tell your doctor about any new or changing skin growth, or a sore that does not heal.
Thiazide diuretics have been reported to worsen lupus or bring it on.
Sensitivity reactions can happen whether or not you have a history of allergies or asthma.
The most noticeable effect of hydrochlorothiazide is passing urine more often, particularly in the first few weeks.
This is how the medicine works rather than a side effect, and it usually settles as your body adjusts.
Get emergency medical help if you have signs of an allergic reaction, such as hives, difficulty breathing, or swelling of your face, lips, tongue or throat.
Get emergency medical help if you have a severe skin reaction, such as a spreading red or purple rash with blistering and peeling, or skin that is painful to touch.
Stop taking hydrochlorothiazide and get medical help immediately if you have a sudden change in your vision or pain in your eye.
Call your doctor at once if you have:
severe pain in your upper stomach that spreads to your back, with nausea and vomiting, which can be a sign of inflammation of the pancreas (pancreatitis)
yellowing of your skin or the whites of your eyes (jaundice)
fever, chills, sore throat, mouth sores or other signs of infection
unusual bruising or bleeding, or pale skin and unusual tiredness, which can be signs of a blood problem
shortness of breath, wheezing, or a cough with frothy mucus
passing much less urine than usual, or swelling in your legs and ankles
light-headedness or fainting, especially when standing up
signs of dehydration or a salt imbalance, such as extreme thirst, dry mouth, confusion, muscle cramps, irregular heartbeat or unusual weakness
Other hydrochlorothiazide side effects include:
dizziness, a spinning sensation (vertigo), headache, restlessness, or tingling and numbness (paresthesia)
weakness
nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, constipation, stomach cramping, stomach irritation, or loss of appetite
muscle spasm
increased sensitivity to sunlight, causing sunburn more easily
hair loss or thinning
difficulty getting or keeping an erection
temporary blurred vision, or objects looking yellow-tinged (xanthopsia)
swelling and tenderness of the salivary glands
raised blood sugar, sugar in the urine, or raised uric acid
If a side effect is moderate or severe, your doctor may lower your dose or stop the medicine.
Do not stop taking HCTZ on your own without speaking to your doctor first.
This is not a complete list of side effects and others may occur.
Call your doctor for medical advice about side effects.
You may report side effects to the FDA at 1-800-FDA-1088.
Your doctor will choose the smallest dose that controls your condition, and may adjust it over time.
Follow your prescription label and do not change your dose yourself.

sentences.subsection_title: HCTZ dose for high blood pressure (adults)
sentences.sentence: Tablets: The starting dose is hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg once a day, which may be increased to 50 mg a day, taken as a single dose or split into two doses.

sentences.subsection_title: HCTZ dose for high blood pressure (adults)
sentences.sentence: Doses above 50 mg a day are often associated with a marked drop in blood potassium.

sentences.subsection_title: HCTZ dose for high blood pressure (adults)
sentences.sentence: Most people do not need more than 50 mg a day when hydrochlorothiazide is taken alongside other blood pressure medicines

sentences.subsection_title: HCTZ dose for high blood pressure (adults)
sentences.sentence: Capsules: The starting dose is a hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg capsule once a day, whether taken on its own or with other blood pressure medicines.

sentences.subsection_title: HCTZ dose for high blood pressure (adults)
sentences.sentence: Total daily doses above 50 mg are not recommended.

sentences.subsection_title: HCTZ dose for high blood pressure (adults)
sentences.sentence: Capsules are approved for high blood pressure only, not for fluid retention.
Tablets : The usual dose is hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg to 100 mg a day, taken as a single dose or split into two doses.
Many people with fluid retention respond to intermittent treatment, such as taking it every other day or on 3 to 5 days each week.
Excessive response and undesirable electrolyte imbalance are less likely to occur with intermittent dosing.

sentences.subsection_title: HCTZ dose for children for high blood pressure and fluid retention
sentences.sentence: The usual HCTZ dose in children, for both high blood pressure and fluid retention, is 1 mg to 2 mg per kilogram of body weight (0.5 mg to 1 mg per pound) a day, given as a single dose or split into two doses.

sentences.subsection_title: HCTZ dose for children for high blood pressure and fluid retention
sentences.sentence: Infants under 6 months: may be need doses of up to 3 mg per kilogram (1.5 mg per pound) a day, given as two divided doses up to the same maximum 37.5 mg daily limit

sentences.subsection_title: HCTZ dose for children for high blood pressure and fluid retention
sentences.sentence: Infants and children under 2 years: do not exceed 37.5 mg a day

sentences.subsection_title: HCTZ dose for children for high blood pressure and fluid retention
sentences.sentence: Children 2 to 12 years: do not exceed 100 mg a day

sentences.subsection_title: HCTZ dose for children for high blood pressure and fluid retention
sentences.sentence: The dose is based on your child's weight and must be worked out by their doctor.
If your child has been prescribed the liquid form (oral suspension), the following applies:
Shake the bottle well before every dose.
Measure each dose with the oral dosing syringe.
Ask your pharmacist for a syringe and a bottle adapter if you do not have them.
Never measure a dose with a household teaspoon or tablespoon, because these do not give an accurate amount.
Store the made-up suspension at room temperature and do not freeze it.
Throw away any unused suspension 30 days after it was made up.
The pharmacist will write this date on the bottle.
The oral suspension can be taken with or without food.

sentences.subsection_title: What happens if I miss a dose?
sentences.sentence: Take the medicine as soon as you can, but skip the missed dose if it is almost time for your next dose.

sentences.subsection_title: What happens if I miss a dose?
sentences.sentence: Do not take two doses at one time.
Seek emergency medical attention or call the Poison Help line at 1-800-222-1222.
Overdose symptoms may include nausea , dizziness , dry mouth, thirst, and muscle pain or weakness.

sentences.section_title: What other drugs will affect hydrochlorothiazide?
sentences.sentence: Tell your doctor and pharmacist about all the medicines you take, including prescription and over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, and herbal products.

sentences.section_title: What other drugs will affect hydrochlorothiazide?
sentences.sentence: Lithium.

sentences.section_title: What other drugs will affect hydrochlorothiazide?
sentences.sentence: Lithium and diuretics generally should not be taken together.

sentences.section_title: What other drugs will affect hydrochlorothiazide?
sentences.sentence: Hydrochlorothiazide reduces how quickly the kidneys clear lithium, which carries a high risk of lithium toxicity.

sentences.section_title: What other drugs will affect hydrochlorothiazide?
sentences.sentence: Cholestyramine and colestipol.

sentences.section_title: What other drugs will affect hydrochlorothiazide?
sentences.sentence: These cholesterol-lowering resins bind hydrochlorothiazide in the gut and can reduce how much you absorb by up to 85 percent for cholestyramine and 43 percent for colestipol.

sentences.section_title: What other drugs will affect hydrochlorothiazide?
sentences.sentence: The doses need to be separated.

sentences.section_title: What other drugs will affect hydrochlorothiazide?
sentences.sentence: For the oral suspension, the label advises taking hydrochlorothiazide at least 4 hours before, or 4 to 6 hours after, the resin.

sentences.section_title: What other drugs will affect hydrochlorothiazide?
sentences.sentence: NSAIDs such as ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin), naproxen (Aleve), diclofenac, meloxicam, indomethacin, celecoxib and aspirin.

sentences.section_title: What other drugs will affect hydrochlorothiazide?
sentences.sentence: These can reduce the fluid-clearing and blood-pressure-lowering effects of hydrochlorothiazide, and your doctor will check whether the medicine is still working as intended.

sentences.section_title: What other drugs will affect hydrochlorothiazide?
sentences.sentence: Insulin and oral diabetes medicines.

sentences.section_title: What other drugs will affect hydrochlorothiazide?
sentences.sentence: Your diabetes medicine dose may need adjusting.

sentences.section_title: What other drugs will affect hydrochlorothiazide?
sentences.sentence: Corticosteroids and ACTH.

sentences.section_title: What other drugs will affect hydrochlorothiazide?
sentences.sentence: Taken with hydrochlorothiazide, these increase the loss of salts from the body, particularly potassium.

sentences.section_title: What other drugs will affect hydrochlorothiazide?
sentences.sentence: Digoxin and other digitalis medicines.

sentences.section_title: What other drugs will affect hydrochlorothiazide?
sentences.sentence: Low potassium caused by hydrochlorothiazide can make the heart more sensitive to the toxic effects of digitalis, including irregular heart rhythms.

sentences.section_title: What other drugs will affect hydrochlorothiazide?
sentences.sentence: Other blood pressure medicines.

sentences.section_title: What other drugs will affect hydrochlorothiazide?
sentences.sentence: The effects add together, which may be intended, but can also lower blood pressure more than expected.

sentences.section_title: What other drugs will affect hydrochlorothiazide?
sentences.sentence: Alcohol, barbiturates and opioid pain medicines.

sentences.section_title: What other drugs will affect hydrochlorothiazide?
sentences.sentence: These can make the drop in blood pressure on standing worse, causing dizziness or fainting.

sentences.section_title: What other drugs will affect hydrochlorothiazide?
sentences.sentence: Muscle relaxants used during surgery (nondepolarizing muscle relaxants such as tubocurarine).

sentences.section_title: What other drugs will affect hydrochlorothiazide?
sentences.sentence: You may respond more strongly to them, so tell your surgeon and anesthetist that you take hydrochlorothiazide.

sentences.section_title: What other drugs will affect hydrochlorothiazide?
sentences.sentence: Medicines that raise blood pressure (pressor amines such as norepinephrine).

sentences.section_title: What other drugs will affect hydrochlorothiazide?
sentences.sentence: Your response to them may be reduced, although this does not usually prevent their use.

sentences.section_title: What other drugs will affect hydrochlorothiazide?
sentences.sentence: This list is not complete.

sentences.section_title: What other drugs will affect hydrochlorothiazide?
sentences.sentence: Other medicines may affect hydrochlorothiazide, and hydrochlorothiazide may affect other medicines.
